$description: Motion. Two durations and two easings, and nothing else — every enter in this system is the same enter and every leave is the same leave. The values are the ones the Blade components already carry inline as `x-transition ease-out duration-200` / `ease-in duration-150`; naming them is what let the React port stop guessing, because Radix drives its animations from CSS and had no numbers to read.

duration.$description: Asymmetric on purpose: an entrance is an announcement and wants to be seen, a departure is already decided and only has to not snap. 200/150 is the pair the source dashboard converged on.

enter.$description: Anything arriving — a modal, a dropdown, a toast.

leave.$description: Anything going away. Shorter than the enter.

easing.$description: Named for the direction rather than the curve, so a component asks for `ease-enter` and cannot pair an entrance with a decelerating-out curve by accident. NOT named `in`/`out`: Tailwind owns `--ease-in` and `--ease-out` with its own values, and an @theme key overwrites rather than adds.

enter.$description: Decelerating. Fast at the start, settling at the end — the thing arrives and comes to rest.

leave.$description: Accelerating. Eases away and then goes, so the tail of the animation is not the part the reader waits through.
